n: By July 1838 several apostles had left the Church. The Lord directs that a conference be held immediately to reorganize the Twelve and fill the vacancies.

f.g: Apostles such as William E. McLellin, Luke and Lyman Johnson, and John F. Boynton had been excommunicated or had left.

n: Thomas B. Marsh, the quorum president, is to remain in Missouri for a while to publish the Lord’s word.

f.g: Thomas Marsh was involved with the Church’s periodical, the Elders’ Journal.

n: The rest are to begin preaching immediately. If they serve with humility, meekness, and patience, the Lord will provide for their families and open doors for their work.
Next spring they are to cross “the great waters”—the Atlantic—to preach the fulness of the gospel in Great Britain.

They must formally depart from the Far West temple site on April 26, 1839. Though the Saints had been driven from Missouri, several apostles returned secretly at night on that date and fulfilled the command.

f.w: the twenty-sixth day of April next

n: Four new apostles are named: John Taylor, John E. Page, Wilford Woodruff, and Willard Richards. Taylor and Woodruff would later become Presidents of the Church.

f.g: Fourth President of the Church (1889–1898); he issued the Manifesto (Official Declaration 1).
